hook: SCP-705 is one of the lighter files in the canon: a tub of red modeling clay that turns into a tiny, deadly serious army whenever someone takes the lid off. Go in expecting a short read whose humor comes from the gap between military ambition and complete harmlessness. The clinical tone never cracks, and that is exactly what makes it funny.
whyItMatters: It shows how a Safe-class report can work as comedy without ever announcing a joke. The containment rules are about access logs and penalties for whoever forgets to close the lid, which tells you the real hazard is staff carelessness rather than the object. The premise, toy soldiers with real ambitions, can be explained in one sentence and remembered after one read.
thingsToNotice: The escalation is all about scale: the clay figures organize, produce leaders, and eventually sculpt tanks, helicopters and bombers, yet every one of them still fires harmless clay rounds. Touching other tubs of modeling compound spawns rival armies sorted by color, complete with alliances and casualties, so one unattended desk could host a small world war. The closing addendum is the payoff: the very first campaign captured a break-room coffee maker and proclaimed it independent territory, until a researcher swept the troops off the burner and broke them. The detail that the survivors still talk about that day with fear and resentment gives the clay soldiers a shared memory, which is both silly and a little sad.
